analysis_steps.goal: Analyze 6.7 GHz methanol maser variability, velocity drifts, and periodicity

method.value: Extract integrated flux density and peak velocity time series for five maser features from HartRAO single-dish monitoring; fit velocity drifts with linear regression; fit exponential decay to the +11.45 km s^-1 feature; determine periodicity using Period04 and Lomb-Scargle periodogram; compute relative amplitude variations.

evidence.quote: Linear regression analysis is applied to each velocity time series to determine the velocity drift, and the results are included in this table.
The period of each is determined using, firstly the programme Period04 developed by (cite: lenz2004period04) and secondly the Lomb-Scargle (LS) periodigram (cite: scargle82).
Finally, for $v_{LSR} =$+11.45 km s$^{-1}$, it is possible to fit an exponentially decaying function to the flux density time series, see Fig. 4.

key_parameters.value: Five velocity features: +8.42, +9.65, +10.44, +10.70, and +11.45 km s^-1

evidence.quote: For the purpose of analysis of these observations five features, two at $v_{LSR} =$+10.44 and +10.70 km s$^{-1}$ in the heavily line merged velocity regime, and others at $v_{LSR} =$+8.42, +9.65, and +11.45 km s$^{-1}$ are selected.

fitting.value: Linear regression on velocity time series (goodness of fit R^2 > 50% for measurable drift) and exponential decay fit F_Int_6.7 = a * e^(MJD/b) + c

evidence.quote: Two of the features have measurable velocity drifts, with "goodness of fit" values R$^{2} >$ 50$\%$.
Finally, for $v_{LSR} =$+11.45 km s$^{-1}$, it is possible to fit an exponentially decaying function to the flux density time series, see Fig. 4.

findings_qualitative.value: G188.95+0.89 is resolved into eight 1.3 mm dust continuum cores (MM1-MM8), with MM1 being the brightest and associated with the periodic 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser source.

evidence.quote: G188.95$+$0.89 protocluster is resolved into eight 1.3 mm objects (MM1-MM8). MM1 and MM2 are the central objects and MM1 (the brightest dust continuum object) is associated with the periodic 6.7 GHz CH$_3$OH maser source.

findings_qualitative.value: All five selected 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser features are periodic with no detectable phase lags, while the +11.45 km s^-1 feature decays exponentially from 2003 and two features (+9.65 and +11.45 km s^-1) show measurable velocity drifts.

evidence.quote: In these observations five features are periodically varying and at least two exhibit evidence of velocity drifts.
The 11.45 km s$^{-1}$ feature has decreased exponentially from 2003.
No phase lags between maser features were found.

findings_qualitative.value: MM2 likely hosts at least a binary YSO system, evidenced by two continuum cores separated by 0.1 arcsec in ALMA Band 7, double-peaked CH3OH emission, and multiple outflow orientations in 12CO.

evidence.quote: First, the high-resolution ALMA band 7 dust continuum image resolves MM2 into 2 cores separated by 0.1$"$.

An east-west outflow feature with an axis through the peak position of MM2, as well as a north-west and south-east outflow also intersecting with MM2, can be observed. These support the suggestion at least a binary system is present in MM2.

findings_qualitative.value: SiO emission exhibits a bow-shock morphology in the north-west region of MM2, and C18O emission is brightest at the interface between MM1 and MM2.

evidence.quote: The dominant SiO emission is observed in the north-west region of MM2, see Fig. 7. The emission has a bow-shock morphology in the channel corresponding to the systemic velocity of MM2.
Interestingly, the brightest C$^{18}$O ($J=2-1$) channel (3  km s$^{-1}$ channel) show a distribution of the C$^{18}$O ($J=2-1$) emission to lie in the interface between MM1 and MM2 cores.

claims.hypothesis: The 6.7 GHz CH3OH maser features in G188.95+0.89 share a common periodic modulation around the revised 395 d period and exhibit long-term velocity drifts.
claims.experiment: Monitored the 6.7 GHz CH3OH masers with the HartRAO 26-m telescope from 2003 to 2021 and analyzed five velocity features using Period04, Lomb-Scargle periodograms, and linear regression.
claims.result: All five features are periodic with average periods of 395 ± 1 d (Period04) and 397.6 ± 0.7 d (Lomb-Scargle), no phase lags are found, and two features (+9.65 and +11.45 km s^-1) show linear velocity drifts with R^2 > 50%.
claims.finding: The shorter ~395 d period is confirmed across all five features, suggesting a common background source of seed photons (possibly protostellar pulsation), while two features experience measurable velocity drifts.

evidence.loc: Implications of the variability in the 6.7 GHz CH3OH Masers
evidence.quote: Here, using the longer time series and from two separate methods, the shorter period is confirmed ($\tau_{Period04}=395\pm1$ d and $\tau_{LS}=397.6\pm0.7$ d).
All five features are periodic, suggesting a common background source of seed photon.
Two CH$_3$OH maser features are reported with measurable velocity drift.

claims.hypothesis: G188.95+0.89 hosts a fragmented massive protocluster at millimeter wavelengths.
claims.experiment: Imaged ALMA Band 6 1.3 mm dust continuum emission and calculated core masses assuming optically thin dust.
claims.result: Eight 1.3 mm continuum cores (MM1-MM8) are resolved with masses ranging from 0.4 to 8.2 M_odot, with MM1 (8.2 M_odot) associated with the 6.7 GHz methanol maser site.
claims.finding: G188.95+0.89 is resolved into eight 1.3 mm continuum cores, with MM1 and MM2 as the central dominant cores.

evidence.quote: G188.95$+$0.89 protocluster is resolved into eight 1.3 mm objects (MM1-MM8). MM1 and MM2 are the central objects and MM1 (the brightest dust continuum object) is associated with the periodic 6.7 GHz CH$_3$OH maser source.

claims.hypothesis: Core MM2 hosts a binary or multiple young stellar object system.
claims.experiment: Examined ALMA Band 7 continuum contours and Band 6 CH3OH (4_(2,2)-3_(1,2)), SiO, and 12CO (2-1) line emission and spectra towards MM2.
claims.result: Band 7 continuum resolves MM2 into two cores separated by 0.1 arcsec; CH3OH emission towards MM2 is double-peaked; 12CO traces both an east-west bipolar outflow and emission north/north-west and south-east of MM2.
claims.finding: Multiple indicators support the presence of at least a binary YSO system in MM2, though higher-resolution continuum and line observations are needed to test multiplicity further.

evidence.quote: First, the high-resolution ALMA band 7 dust continuum image resolves MM2 into 2 cores separated by 0.1$"$. Second, the CH$_3$OH (4$_{(2,2)}-$3$_{(1,2)}$) emission is coincident with the systemic velocity and the spectral profile of emission towards MM2 has two pronounced features (see 3 km s$^{-1}$ channel of Fig. 6).

An east-west outflow feature with an axis through the peak position of MM2, as well as a north-west and south-east outflow also intersecting with MM2, can be observed. These support the suggestion at least a binary system is present in MM2.

evidence.quote: However, they also state it may be caused by masers in a precessing disk.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Missing interferometric flux can produce apparent absorption features in 12CO spectra, but the authors consider the observed self-absorption feature towards MM2 to be real cold foreground absorption.

evidence.quote: We noted that missing flux issue can give rise to such spectral feature but in this case the observed absorption feature is real..

limitations_admitted.value: Phase lags between maser features shorter than the 10-20 day observing cadence cannot be measured.

evidence.quote: There may be lags shorter than our cadence that we cannot measure nor speculate about.

limitations_admitted.value: Cores MM5-MM8 lie close to the edge of the primary beam, so their continuum fluxes are not primary-beam corrected and their line emission is affected by decreased sensitivity.

evidence.quote: The integrated flux densities for MM5 to MM8, that were also used in the core mass estimates, are not primary beam corrected since MM5–MM8 are located close to the edge of the primary beam and will not be discussed in detail due to limited sensitivity.
The nature of the emission towards MM5–MM8 is contaminated by the effect of the decreased sensitivity towards the edge of the primary beam.

limitations_admitted.value: Only two maser features show measurable velocity drifts, which is insufficient to make a definitive comparison with disk infall models such as in G9.62+0.20E.

evidence.loc: Implications of the variability in the 6.7 GHz CH3OH Masers
evidence.quote: However, an insufficient number of features with measurable velocity drift are found thus rendering any comparison to G9.62+0.20E indeterminate.

limitations_admitted.value: No direct detection of accretion disks was possible with the current ALMA observations.

evidence.quote: While no direct detection of accretion disks was possible with the current observations, the detected outflows suggest the presence of accretion disks in the source.

ALMA Band 7 continuum data are plotted in Figure 5 and used to claim that MM2 resolves into a 0.1 arcsec binary, but no Band 7 project code, observation details, or data reduction parameters are provided anywhere in the paper.

Section 3.3 promises to discuss the implication of C18O emission at the interface between MM1 and MM2 for the 6.7 GHz maser variability in Section 4.1, but Section 4.1 never mentions C18O.
